messages:
maria: Heads up — we've had two support tickets this week asking why certain enterprise customers keep getting routed to the shared pool during spikes. They claim they set their org header affinity but it doesn’t stick. Can we investigate routing order + fallback behavior?

kevin: Seen that. I think this is the header-evaluation ordering + our 'capacity-fallback' policy. If no matching dedicated capacity, we fall back to shared. But we also have a TTL on header pins (30s) that might expire mid-session.

sam: Quick note: some customers set x-customer-prefer: dedicated in their SDK. We currently read header X-Org-Affinity first, then fallbacks. If they send both headers we prefer org-affinity. Maybe there's ambiguity when proxies normalize case.

julie: Can you paste the snippet of the matcher logic? I want to see the exact precedence.

kevin: Sure — excerpt from the router config:

```
- rules:
  - match:
      header: "x-org-affinity"
      value: "pin"
    action: route_to: "org-pool"
  - match: capacity_available: true
    action: route_to: "org-pool"
  - action: route_to: "shared-pool"
```

kevin: The subtle bug is that proxies sometimes forward header as `x-org-affinity-override` for customers using a custom proxy; our matcher only looks for exact header name.

maria: Oof. So two issues: header normalization and the TTL expiry. We should also add audit logging whenever we fallback from org-pool to shared-pool and tag the event with customer id + reason. Ops asked for this for any enterprise SLA breach.

ira: Adding audit logs sounds right. Also propose a per-org flag in Console: "pin_on_capacity_failure" with three states: "no_pin", "soft_pin" (try org then shared), "hard_pin" (keep queuing or return 503). Could be useful for enterprise contracts.

sam: +1. For hard_pin we need a circuit-breaker in router to avoid starving others — maybe a per-org queue with quotas. We should wire this into quota controller so it counts against their reserved capacity rather than global.

julie: UI question — how would Console surface this? Maybe in Routing > Per-Org > Overrides we show current pin state, TTL, last_fallback (timestamp) and a small "force-demo" toggle for SEs to repro. Also need RBAC so only account owners + SEs can change.

kevin: Implementation plan: 1) Update matcher to canonicalize headers (lowercase + strip proxies). 2) Emit fallback audit event with reason codes (NO_CAPACITY, TTL_EXPIRED, HEADER_MISSING). 3) Add per-org flag (soft/hard/no). 4) Wire quota controller to honor hard_pin. 5) Canary rollout to 5 orgs, monitor latency + token usage.

maria: Sounds good. Who will own the PRs?

kevin: I'll do (1) and (2). Sam picks (3) + quota wiring. Julie can spec Console changes and mockups. Ira can own canary run + alert rules.

ira: For canary metrics, add a telemetry dimension `routing_decision` with values [org_pool, shared_pool, queued, rejected] plus `fallback_reason` tag. Make sure this is exportable to the per-tenant dashboard.

sam: Also add a tiny integ test: simulate header forwarded as `X-Org-Affinity-Override` and TTL expiry. Unit tests + an e2e with the proxy shim.

julie: I'll add UX mocks to Figma and link in the PR description. Need guidance on wording for the flag — "Fallback behavior: allow shared, queue, reject".

maria: Great. Two more asks: include an audit log retention policy (security wants 90 days for routing fallbacks) and include an approval step in the Console when flipping to hard_pin (explicit checkbox + 2-person approval).

kevin: Noted. I'll add retention = 90d and require `assert_admin_approval` for hard_pin change.

ops-bot: deploy queued: router/canonicalize-headers v2 -> staging at 2024-06-12T18:02Z :rocket:

maria: Thanks team — let's aim to get the matcher fix and audit events in this sprint, then follow-up with Console+quota next sprint. :thumbsup:
